newsitem.title: UK: Babcock pays 20.5 mln stg for Rosyth.
newsitem.headline: Babcock pays 20.5 mln stg for Rosyth.

text.p: British engineering firm Babcock International Group Plc said on Thursday it would pay 20.5 million pounds ($34 million) net to buy the UK government's Rosyth Royal Dockyard in Fife, Scotland.
Babcock had commercially managed the dockyard, which has annual sales of over 200 million pounds, since 1987. It announced the acquisition on November 25.

Under the agreement, the Ministry of Defence allocated a 10-year workload to the dockyard, including the refitting of nuclear submarines, aircraft carriers and other vessels, Babcock said in a statement.
The company said it would pay 14.5 million pounds cash upon the deal's completion, which was targeted for early next year.
The gross consideration for the deal was 27 million pounds, before a reduction of 6.5 million to cover the assumption of redundancy liabilities after April 2006.
Babcock said the Ministry of Defence would be liable for substantially all redundancy costs related to the dockyard's present workforce until that time.
The company said the transaction would result in about 5.0 million pounds of negative goodwill on its balance sheet after costs estimated at 1.4 million pounds.
In April, the British government unveiled plans to sell Rosyth's rival dockyard, Devonport in Plymouth, England, to DML, the U.S.-led group that manages the yard.
